interview:
A1: The navigation keeps exactly the five existing section links (about, services, credentials, experience, contact). Do not add, rename, or drop any link, and do not change the visible wording of the medical content.

A2: Clicking a navigation link shows that one section and hides all the others. The page opens on About. Do this with the hidden attribute on the section elements plus the existing section-toggling code in script.js; do not introduce a routing library and do not rewrite the click handling from scratch.

A3: Mark the section you are currently viewing on the navigation itself, using aria-current="page" on the active link and removing it from the others. Semantics only: no colors, no borders, no CSS.

A4: No CSS at all is the hard constraint. No stylesheet file, no <style> block, no style attribute, no CDN or font link. Use plain semantic HTML (a ul/li list inside nav) and the browser's default rendering. On a narrow phone screen it is fine for the list items to stack vertically, because that is what a plain list already does.

A5: Leave the contact form completely as it is: the same field ids, the same validation messages, the same mailto behavior and the same result text. If the form is touched at all, it must still pass the existing repo check in tests/verify-page.mjs.

A6: Scope is index.html and script.js only. Do not create new files, do not add a build step or dependencies, do not modify .factory or factory.yaml, and do not update the docs. A minimal diff that satisfies the five behaviors above is preferred over a rework.
